scope: a functional test, on a CPU toy router, of indicator AST-1: an attention schema (a learned predictor of the router's OWN next routing load, read from its own recent history) that is also used to control routing, against the same router without a schema (FLOP-matched and parameter-matched), an auxiliary-loss-free heuristic balancer, a describe-only schema (trained identically, not used for control) and a router fed the recent load history directly without a separate predictor (the history router). The world is bursty cyclic demand over eight experts of limited capacity with a deterministic verifier; the judged endpoint is the fraction of tokens verified on a fresh evaluation stream, by one-sided 95% t bounds of the paired difference over the declared seeds. The schema has no authority over expert capacity or competence (a structural counter). It makes no claim about consciousness and none about language models or OLMoE routing (the GPU stage B)

Limitations: a result applies to this toy world: eight experts, a cyclic demand of eight regimes of three batches, 256 tokens per batch, capacity 64, a history of four batches and a router of one hidden layer; the schema can only help where the demand is predictable from the router's own load history, which this world builds in on purpose (a stationary world, the null, is run beside it); it says nothing about real routing traces; every tuned configuration (learning rates, entropy coefficients, control-law forms, the balancer step, the step caps) was selected from single draws of the grids on pilot seeds 1001 to 1003, which predate the fix of the initial-weight seeding and are therefore unseeded draws; selection differences of a few per mille (control 901.3 against 899.7) are inside that noise; the heuristic balancer is the schema-free router with an auxiliary-loss-free bias moved by the previous batch's load; its learning rate and step were tuned on pilot seeds on an equal grid; a better-tuned or differently shaped balancer (a predictor-free forecast, an integral term) might close the gap; the schema-free router is matched to the control in FLOPs per batch (the schema's included) and a second one in parameters; neither has the schema's history input, which is the information the schema adds; the history router, which is given the history directly without a separate predictor, IS an arm of this experiment and the one against which the schema's added value is judged (a refutation against it is the expected result, see PREREGISTRATION.md); the schema is trained by its prediction loss alone, detached from the policy: a joint training, or a schema that sees more than the router's own load history, is another experiment; recovery after an expert is revoked or overloaded, and routing churn between policy versions beyond the descriptive probe, are not judged at stage A; the t bounds assume roughly normal paired differences, which the declared seeds cannot check; per-seed differences, medians and both bounds are reported; the shuffled-history attribution reads whether the gain depends on the router's own recent history; it is judged: a supported contrast whose shuffled-history control is not ATTRIBUTED is NOT_SHOWN; an indicator property here is a functional property: the experiment says nothing about whether any system is conscious.
